title: How to Price Digital Products: A Simple Framework
seoTitle: How to Price Digital Products: A Simple Framework
description: A practical framework for pricing ebooks, templates and planners using value, costs and customer feedback.
imageAlt: A guide to setting a price for a digital product

blocks.text: Pricing should communicate value, support sustainable creation and make sense for your audience. Define the outcome: what task does the product help complete, how much time might it save and what uncertainty does it reduce?

Understand customers and alternatives. Compare products with similar audiences, depth, quality and support. Include free alternatives; your paid offer should provide a clearer, more specific or more useful solution.

Calculate your cost floor. Include creation time, software, research, contractors, advertising, payment processing, platform fees and customer support. Estimate how many sales recover creation and maintenance costs.

Choose a model that fits. One-time pricing suits a standalone resource. Tiers work when versions have meaningful differences. Bundles should solve related problems. Subscriptions require ongoing value or updates.
Test a credible starting price. Make discounts intentional and time-limited. If testing prices, change one variable at a time and compare similar audiences.

Review what you retain. Gross sales are not take-home earnings. Deduct payment-provider charges, platform fees and fixed plan costs; also consider refunds, discounts, business expenses and taxes on your own sales. CloverLoop's calculator estimates selected costs only.
Only if it is a deliberate, time-limited validation offer.
It should deliver a coherent additional outcome.
How often should I change price?
When meaningful evidence from feedback, conversion or costs supports it.
No. It excludes many business expenses and tax liabilities.
